review.market_summary: Three themes matter right now. (1) Strong jobs data: October payrolls came in at +165k, above every forecast, and unemployment fell to 4.1%. That is a fresh hawkish shock that should push out rate-cut expectations. (2) Risk-off after the midterms: the Democratic sweep set off a sharp AI and semiconductor sell-off (SMH -20%, NVDA -15%, QQQ -9.5% in 5 days), reports of global contagion, and a looming debt-ceiling fight. Haven buying has kept bonds bid (TLT +0.5%) even before the jobs print is fully priced. (3) Oil is caught between two forces. Prices are heading for a sharp weekly drop (USO -12%), while Iran/Strait of Hormuz headlines are still speculative ('could push oil past $100'). The cleanest trade is rates. Equity signals are mostly late, since they would mean shorting tech after it has already crashed or buying cyclicals into a falling market. I'm taking only two small, sized-down positions.
